periods.analysis: We closed 2024-Q3 with 2 FAA-reportable aviation safety incidents, which is green against the target of <=3 and gives us a solid operating baseline for this series. I am reading that result in the context of peak summer passenger volumes, heavier international turns, and added cargo activity on the east ramp, not as an invitation to relax. Both events were taken through the Safety Management System review board, with emphasis on Taxiway B hold-short discipline and ramp movements around Gates C11-C16. The important point is that the airport stayed inside tolerance while surfacing the exact places where growth puts pressure on procedures.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 0430 operations huddle, daily FOD sweep, and joint airfield-ramp safety walk that kept summer activity disciplined. Extend recurrent ramp-driver coaching to the C-concourse ground handlers and require supervisors to document two observed pushbacks per shift through October. Keep the Taxiway B hotspot on the weekly safety board until we have two more clean quarters of observation data.

periods.analysis: In 2024-Q4 we recorded 1 FAA-reportable incident, a decrease of 1 from 2 in 2024-Q3, and we remained green against the <=3 target. That improvement came during the holiday travel window, which tells me the winter readiness work, snow desk coordination, and airline station briefings had real operational value. The single reportable event was closed with corrective action focused on ground-equipment positioning on the north cargo apron. I like the direction, but I do not treat a count of 1 as luck; I treat it as a process to be protected.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the winter-operations playbook that tied Airport Operations, ARFF, deicing vendors, and airline duty managers into one command rhythm. Extend equipment telematics review to the north cargo apron tugs and belt loaders, with exception reports reviewed every Friday by Airfield Ops. Before the next holiday peak, rerun the tabletop on low-visibility taxi routing for Taxiways K and L.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q1 came in at 2 FAA-reportable incidents, an increase of 1 from 1 in 2024-Q4, while still green and within the <=3 target. The quarter carried typical winter friction: deicing queues, migratory bird activity near the infield ponds, and more stop-and-start ground movement during weather holds. The two incidents were reviewed without finding a systemic breakdown, but both pointed to the need for sharper handoffs between ramp control and airline ground crews during irregular operations. The story is still positive, but the margin narrowed enough to deserve attention.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the snow desk and daily safety huddle, because they are preventing weather disruption from becoming safety drift. Extend the wildlife patrol overlap on dawn shifts along Runway 10/28 and log dispersal activity by zone so we can see whether the pond-edge treatments are working. Require a 15-minute ramp-control refresher for supervisors on all carriers with more than eight daily turns before the spring schedule change.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q2 the count rose to 3 FAA-reportable incidents, an increase of 1 from 2 in 2025-Q1, which is still green but exactly at our <=3 ceiling. This is the quarter where I want the organization to hear both halves of the sentence: compliant, and with no cushion. Spring construction on the west taxilane, higher general aviation training activity, and compressed gate turns around the international bank all increased the number of interfaces where a small miss can become reportable. Corrective actions were opened on contractor escort discipline, temporary marking visibility, and ramp radio phraseology.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the construction safety briefings, but move them from twice weekly to daily while the west taxilane closure remains active. Extend escort requirements so every contractor vehicle crossing the movement-area boundary carries a live transponder and a named airport escort, not just a company badge. Put temporary Taxiway J and west-ramp markings on a night inspection checklist until the project is demobilized.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q3 improved to 2 FAA-reportable incidents, a decrease of 1 from 3 in 2025-Q2, returning us from the edge of the target back into a healthier green position. That is the result I expected after tightening construction escorts, refreshing radio phraseology, and adding night inspections on the west taxilane work zone. Summer passenger volume was strong, so the lower count suggests the controls held under real pressure rather than benefiting from lighter activity. I am especially encouraged that the ramp audit team found fewer repeat findings around temporary markings and vehicle staging.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the daily construction safety brief until final pavement acceptance, then convert the highest-value items into the standing airfield inspection protocol. Extend the successful radio-phraseology refresh to cargo operators and fixed-base operator tenants before the fall freight build. Keep publishing a one-page weekly hotspot map for Gates B7-B14 and the west ramp so supervisors can brief crews before first push.

periods.analysis: For 2025-Q4 we held at 2 FAA-reportable incidents, with no change from 2 in 2025-Q3, and remained green against the <=3 target. Flat performance during holiday peaks, early fog mornings, and a heavier overnight cargo bank is a disciplined result. The two events clustered around overnight ramp movements rather than runway operations, which helps us focus the next layer of prevention. The broader arc from 2025-Q2 is that the airport absorbed growth and construction pressure without letting the incident count run away.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the weekly hotspot map and add an overnight edition for cargo ramp leads working the 2300-0400 push. Extend supervisor ride-alongs to the third-shift ground-service crews at the north cargo apron, with findings logged in the SMS action tracker. Use the January airline station-manager meeting to confirm that holiday seasonal hires completed ramp-driver and wing-walker modules, not just general onboarding.

periods.analysis: 2026-Q1 again recorded 2 FAA-reportable incidents, no change from 2 in 2025-Q4, keeping us green and within the <=3 target. The stability matters because the quarter included deicing operations, crosswind days, and several weather-driven gate swaps that can test communication discipline. Our controls are now showing repeatability: daily huddles, hotspot mapping, wildlife tracking, and ramp supervisor observations are becoming the way we run the airport, not special campaigns. Still, two incidents are two too many, and the next improvement will come from reducing variation in overnight and irregular-operation handoffs.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the full SMS cadence and protect the time for incident-closeout reviews within five business days of each report. Extend the overnight cargo ramp ride-along program for one more quarter and compare findings against Q4 to confirm whether behaviors are changing. Add a brief deicing-to-ramp-control handoff checklist for weather days, with spot checks by the Airport Operations duty manager.

periods.analysis: In 2026-Q2 the count increased to 3 FAA-reportable incidents, up 1 from 2 in 2026-Q1, so we are still green but again sitting right at the <=3 target. I am comfortable that the system is functioning, because the incidents were reported promptly and entered the SMS review stream, but I am not comfortable with operating at the ceiling. The quarter combined spring thunderstorms, runway-lighting maintenance windows, and a busy international schedule, all of which put more stress on sequencing and surface movement. This is the moment to tighten execution before a green measure turns into a warning signal.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the current reporting culture and make clear to tenants that timely reporting remains non-negotiable, even when the count is uncomfortable. Extend temporary maintenance-window coordination by requiring a same-day field condition briefing for tower, Airport Operations, ARFF, and affected carriers whenever lighting or pavement work changes taxi routing. Launch a 30-day surface-movement emphasis on Taxiways B, J, and K, with daily review of hold-short compliance and ramp-control recordings.

periods.analysis: FAA-reportable aviation incidents decreased from three to two, below the ceiling of three. Continue to treat prompt reporting and surface-movement review as essential despite the favorable count.
periods.recommendations: Maintain field-condition briefings during lighting and pavement work and review any repeat taxi-routing hazards.
